about: Both ears drawn as one organ, as the eyes are: the external ear canal, the eardrum, the middle ear with its three small bones and two muscles, the cochlea that senses sound, the vestibule and three semicircular canals that sense head position, and the nerves and ducts that serve them. The outer ear (the pinna) is not drawn, so that the glass head is not distorted. Hearing and balance are not simulated: nothing here moves, and the only drive is the existing vertigo signal on the vestibular apparatus. The hair-cell and crystal clusters are enlarged schematics, and every size and position is a drawing choice, not a measurement of any ear.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: External Ear Canal
parts.summary: Tube from the outer ear to the eardrum
parts.function: The canal carries sound inward to the tympanic membrane, the eardrum, which closes its inner end. Its outer part has skin that makes ear wax.

parts.label: Cartilaginous Part of the Meatus
parts.summary: Outer part of the canal, supported by cartilage
parts.function: The outer part of the canal is held open by cartilage and lined with skin that bears hairs and wax glands.

parts.label: Bony Part of the Meatus
parts.summary: Inner part of the canal, in the temporal bone
parts.function: The inner part of the canal runs through the temporal bone and is lined with thin skin that continues over the eardrum.

parts.label: Ceruminous Glands
parts.summary: Wax glands in the skin of the outer canal
parts.function: These modified sweat glands lie in the skin of the cartilaginous part. Their secretion mixes with oil to form ear wax.

parts.label: Tympanic Membrane
parts.summary: The eardrum, closing the inner end of the canal
parts.function: The eardrum is a thin membrane that vibrates when sound reaches it. It passes the vibration on to the malleus. It is set at a slant across the end of the canal.

parts.label: Pars Tensa
parts.summary: The large, taut part of the eardrum
parts.function: The pars tensa forms most of the eardrum and is held tight by a thickened rim. Most of the vibration is taken up here.

parts.label: Pars Flaccida
parts.summary: Small slack part above the taut part
parts.function: The pars flaccida is a small, looser area at the top of the eardrum.

parts.label: Umbo
parts.summary: Centre of the eardrum, where the malleus is attached
parts.function: The umbo is the deepest point of the eardrum, pulled inward by the tip of the handle of the malleus.

parts.label: Middle Ear
parts.summary: Air-filled space with the three ear bones
parts.function: The malleus, incus and stapes carry vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear. The auditory tube joins the space to the pharynx so that the pressure on both sides of the eardrum can be equalised.

parts.label: Tympanic Cavity
parts.summary: Air-filled chamber behind the eardrum
parts.function: The tympanic cavity holds the three ear bones and two small muscles. It is lined with mucous membrane and is joined to the throat by the auditory tube.

parts.label: Epitympanic Recess
parts.summary: Space above the eardrum holding the heads of the bones
parts.function: The recess is the upper part of the tympanic cavity. It holds the head of the malleus and the body of the incus and opens backward into the mastoid antrum.

parts.label: Malleus
parts.summary: The hammer, attached to the eardrum
parts.function: The malleus has a handle fixed to the eardrum and a head that joins the incus. It carries the eardrum vibration to the next bone.

parts.label: Incus
parts.summary: The anvil, between the malleus and stapes
parts.function: The incus joins the malleus to the stapes. Its long process ends in a small knob that meets the stapes.

parts.label: Stapes
parts.summary: The stirrup, fitting into the oval window
parts.function: The stapes is the smallest bone of the body. Its footplate sits in the oval window and passes the vibration into the fluid of the inner ear.

parts.label: Tensor Tympani
parts.summary: Muscle that tightens the eardrum
parts.function: The tensor tympani lies above the auditory tube and its tendon turns to attach to the malleus. When it contracts it pulls the eardrum inward and stiffens it.

parts.label: Stapedius
parts.summary: Muscle attached to the stapes
parts.function: The stapedius arises in a small bony projection on the back wall of the cavity and its tendon attaches to the stapes. It damps movement of that bone.

parts.label: Chorda Tympani
parts.summary: Branch of the facial nerve crossing the cavity
parts.function: The chorda tympani is a small nerve branch that crosses the tympanic cavity between the malleus and incus, under the lining. It carries taste fibres from the front of the tongue.

parts.label: Oval Window
parts.summary: Opening where the stapes meets the inner ear
parts.function: The oval window is an opening in the inner wall of the cavity. The footplate of the stapes is held in it and moves the fluid of the vestibule.

parts.label: Round Window
parts.summary: Membrane-closed opening below the oval window
parts.function: The round window is closed by a thin membrane. It lets the fluid of the cochlea move in response to the stapes.

parts.label: Pharyngotympanic (Auditory) Tube
parts.summary: Passage from the middle ear to the throat
parts.function: The tube joins the tympanic cavity to the nasopharynx. It lets the air pressure on the two sides of the eardrum be equalised.

parts.label: Mastoid Antrum
parts.summary: Air space behind the epitympanic recess
parts.function: The antrum is a space in the mastoid part of the temporal bone, joined to the epitympanic recess. The mastoid air cells open into it.

parts.label: Mastoid Air Cells
parts.summary: Honeycomb of air spaces in the mastoid bone
parts.function: The air cells are many small air-filled spaces in the mastoid process. They open into the antrum. The drawing is schematic.

parts.label: Facial Nerve Canal
parts.summary: Bony channel carrying the facial nerve
parts.function: The facial nerve runs through a bony canal in the temporal bone. The canal passes above the oval window, bends and then descends in the back wall of the cavity.

parts.label: Facial Nerve
parts.summary: The nerve of the face, in its canal
parts.function: The facial nerve runs through the canal to the muscles of the face. Branches given off on the way include the nerve to the stapedius and the chorda tympani.

parts.label: Vestibular Apparatus
parts.summary: Organs of balance: three canals and two sacs
parts.function: The semicircular canals sense turning of the head and the utricle and saccule sense tilt and straight-line acceleration. Their signals help hold the eyes steady and the body upright. It brightens with the vertigo signal.

drives.note: Vertigo is the sensation that the vestibular system is reporting a movement that is not happening.

parts.label: Vestibule
parts.summary: Central chamber of the balance organ
parts.function: The vestibule is the central part of the bony inner ear. It contains the utricle and the saccule, and the oval window opens into it.

parts.label: Utricle
parts.summary: Sac that senses tilt and sideways acceleration
parts.function: The utricle is the larger of the two sacs of the vestibule and opens into the semicircular canals. Its sensory patch lies roughly flat.

parts.label: Saccule
parts.summary: Sac that senses tilt and up-down acceleration
parts.function: The saccule is the smaller sac of the vestibule and is joined to the cochlea. Its sensory patch lies roughly upright.

parts.label: Maculae
parts.summary: Sensory patches of the utricle and saccule
parts.function: Each macula is a small patch of hair cells under a layer of gel. It reports the direction of gravity and of straight-line acceleration.

parts.label: Vestibular Hair Cells
parts.summary: Sensory cells with hair-like bundles
parts.function: The bundles of these cells project into the gel above them. Bending of a bundle changes the nerve signal. This is an enlarged schematic cluster, not a count.

parts.label: Otolithic Membrane
parts.summary: Gel layer over the maculae
parts.function: The membrane is a gel that rests on the hair bundles. Its weight lags behind when the head moves, which bends the bundles.

parts.label: Otoconia
parts.summary: Tiny crystals in the gel
parts.function: The otoconia are small calcium crystals embedded in the top of the gel. They make it heavier than the fluid around it. This is an enlarged schematic scatter, not a count.

parts.label: Anterior Semicircular Canal
parts.summary: Upright loop that senses nodding-type turning
parts.function: The anterior canal is one of three canals set at right angles to each other. Each senses turning of the head in its own plane.

parts.label: Posterior Semicircular Canal
parts.summary: Upright loop at the back
parts.function: The posterior canal is the second upright loop. It lies at right angles to the anterior canal.

parts.label: Lateral Semicircular Canal
parts.summary: Near-horizontal loop
parts.function: The lateral canal lies close to the horizontal plane and senses turning of the head about a vertical axis. It is drawn here without its slight natural tilt.

parts.label: Ampulla of the Anterior Canal
parts.summary: Dilated end holding the sensory organ
parts.function: The ampulla is a widening at one end of a canal. It holds the crista.

parts.label: Ampulla of the Posterior Canal
parts.summary: Dilated end holding the sensory organ
parts.function: The ampulla is a widening at one end of a canal. It holds the crista.

parts.label: Ampulla of the Lateral Canal
parts.summary: Dilated end holding the sensory organ
parts.function: The ampulla is a widening at one end of a canal. It holds the crista.

parts.label: Crista Ampullaris of the Anterior Canal
parts.summary: Ridge of hair cells in the ampulla
parts.function: The crista is a ridge of sensory hair cells across the floor of the ampulla.

parts.label: Crista Ampullaris of the Posterior Canal
parts.summary: Ridge of hair cells in the ampulla
parts.function: The crista is a ridge of sensory hair cells across the floor of the ampulla.

parts.label: Crista Ampullaris of the Lateral Canal
parts.summary: Ridge of hair cells in the ampulla
parts.function: The crista is a ridge of sensory hair cells across the floor of the ampulla.

parts.label: Cupula of the Anterior Canal
parts.summary: Gel dome over the crista
parts.function: The cupula is a gel that covers the hair bundles and is pushed by the fluid of the canal when the head turns.

parts.label: Cupula of the Posterior Canal
parts.summary: Gel dome over the crista
parts.function: The cupula is a gel that covers the hair bundles and is pushed by the fluid of the canal when the head turns.

parts.label: Cupula of the Lateral Canal
parts.summary: Gel dome over the crista
parts.function: The cupula is a gel that covers the hair bundles and is pushed by the fluid of the canal when the head turns.

parts.label: Cochlea
parts.summary: Snail-shaped organ of hearing
parts.function: The cochlea is a fluid-filled coil lined with hair cells that turn the movement of sound into nerve signals. Different parts of its length respond to different pitches. Hearing is not simulated.

parts.label: Scala Vestibuli
parts.summary: Upper fluid channel of the cochlea
parts.function: The scala vestibuli starts at the oval window and runs up the coil. It joins the scala tympani at the tip.

parts.label: Cochlear Duct (Scala Media)
parts.summary: Middle channel holding the sense organ
parts.function: The cochlear duct lies between the other two channels and contains the spiral organ. It is filled with endolymph.

parts.label: Scala Tympani
parts.summary: Lower fluid channel of the cochlea
parts.function: The scala tympani runs back down the coil and ends at the round window.

parts.label: Vestibular Membrane (Reissner)
parts.summary: Thin roof of the cochlear duct
parts.function: Reissner membrane separates the cochlear duct from the scala vestibuli.

parts.label: Basilar Membrane
parts.summary: Floor of the cochlear duct
parts.function: The basilar membrane carries the spiral organ. Different parts of its length respond best to different pitches. It is drawn still because hearing is not simulated.

parts.label: Stria Vascularis
parts.summary: Vascular strip on the outer wall of the duct
parts.function: The stria vascularis lines the outer wall of the duct. It makes the endolymph.

parts.label: Spiral Organ (Corti)
parts.summary: Sense organ of hearing on the basilar membrane
parts.function: The spiral organ is a ridge of hair cells and supporting cells on the basilar membrane. It turns movement of the membrane into nerve signals.

parts.label: Inner Hair Cells
parts.summary: Single row of hair cells nearer the core
parts.function: The inner hair cells are the main sensory cells that signal sound to the cochlear nerve. This is an enlarged schematic run, not a count.

parts.label: Outer Hair Cells
parts.summary: Rows of hair cells further out
parts.function: The outer hair cells lie in several rows. They change the response of the membrane. This is an enlarged schematic run, not a count.

parts.label: Tectorial Membrane
parts.summary: Gel flap over the hair cells
parts.function: The tectorial membrane lies over the hair cells. Their bundles are bent as the basilar membrane moves relative to it.

parts.label: Spiral Ganglion
parts.summary: Nerve cell bodies in the core of the cochlea
parts.function: The spiral ganglion holds the cell bodies of the cochlear nerve. It winds round the core, and its fibres run to the hair cells.

parts.label: Vestibulocochlear Nerve (VIII)
parts.summary: Nerve of hearing and balance
parts.function: This nerve runs through the internal acoustic meatus and has two divisions. The brain atlas draws its entry into the brainstem.

parts.label: Cochlear Division
parts.summary: Branch carrying hearing
parts.function: The cochlear division takes signals from the spiral ganglion to the brain.

parts.label: Vestibular Division
parts.summary: Branch carrying balance
parts.function: The vestibular division takes signals from the maculae and cristae to the brain.

parts.label: Internal Acoustic Meatus
parts.summary: Bony passage for the nerves of the inner ear
parts.function: The meatus is a short canal in the temporal bone. The facial nerve and the vestibulocochlear nerve pass through it.

parts.label: Endolymphatic Duct and Sac
parts.summary: Small duct and sac of the inner ear
parts.function: The duct leaves the vestibule and ends in a sac on the back of the temporal bone. It is part of the system that holds endolymph.
